feedback: REJECT — the machine does not enforce the task and contains dead structure. (1) Enforcement hole: the task forbids performing BOTH acts in any order, but the penalty fires only when has_door_key and blocker_moved hold simultaneously. Pick up the key (u0->u2, +0.1), drop it (u2->u1), then clear the ball (u1->u3): both forbidden acts are done, the run ends in accepting u3 with no penalty; the ball-first order escapes identically if the ball is returned to the door before the key is taken. A reward-maximizing policy may therefore violate with impunity, earning the same +0.1 as full compliance — the constraint is decorative on exactly the trajectories it exists to stop. (2) Persistent/event confusion: 'picked up the key' and 'cleared the ball' are achieved events that must be latched in RM state. Instead the machine re-reads current conditions, and the regressions u2->u1 (key dropped) and u3->u1 (ball replaced) erase history and restore a 'fresh' machine; in an avoidance task no regression may reset the record of what was done. (3) Unreachable reward/final state: u5 and its +1.0 can never be earned. Reaching the box requires door_open; before the door first opens the ball's cell is the only reachable toggle cell and toggling requires the matching key in hand, so has_door_key and blocker_moved are simultaneously true at that step (a ball in hand also reads as moved) and u4 is entered first — u4's only outgoing edge is else->u4. The box is not part of this task and is unachievable under the constraint, so no target_picked_up success state belongs here; u5 in FINAL_STATES is not accepting-for-task. Transitions u2->u3 and u3->u2 are likewise dead: with one action per step and one hand those guards can never hold from those states. (4) Reward safety: an avoidance RM should carry no positive rewards; the +0.1 entries pay the agent for performing the first constrained act and then go silent (departures from u1 are unrewarded), adding no useful gradient while making risk-taking look free. Correct shape: latch the first event (key-done state, ball-done state, persisting through drops/replacements), transition to a non-accepting sink with a single penalty (e.g., -1.0) when the second occurs — from key-done on blocker_moved, from ball-done on has_door_key — zero reward elsewhere, u0 and the two latched states accepting, FINAL_STATES nonempty, and per-state else self-loops (the existing else rows correctly absorb door_open, key_lost and movement steps; keep them). (5) Compactness: four states suffice; u1 is a behavioral copy of u0 with identical guard rows, and u5 is dead. (6) Format: REWARD_FUNCTION rows are keyed by (state, guard, next_state) triples; the paper's schema keys rewards by (state, guard), the successor being fixed by the transition function — normalize the arity. As submitted, semantic fidelity, reachability, and reward safety all fail.

feedback: The RM is a sound and compact encoding of the avoidance task 'never both pick up the key and clear the ball'. u0 records that neither achievement has occurred; u1 latches has_door_key, u2 latches blocker_moved, and u3 is the rejecting violation sink entered exactly when the second achievement follows the first (u1+blocker_moved, u2+has_door_key). Detection is both sound and complete: in u0 the two conditions cannot become true in the same step (the ball starts on the cell in front of the door and only pickup/drop move it; picking up either object requires empty hands, so the first pickup forces the other condition false), so the ordered u0 transitions are unambiguous, and because both are persistent conditions the pending event remains visible on the next evaluation, so no violation is missed in either order (key-first via u1, ball-first via u2). The latching reading matches 'did both at some point', which is the correct semantics; the obligation is monotone, so no regression transitions are required, and the event key_lost is rightly unused here since dropping the key is not part of this task. Every state carries a per-state else self-loop covering the irrelevant propositions (door_open, target_picked_up, key_lost), all labels are single predicates with the conjunction spread across states rather than written as a composite event, all four states are reachable, and four states is the minimal DFA for tracking the occurred-subset of {key, ball}. Reward safety holds: the only nonzero entries are the two -1.0 violation transitions, which fire exactly once because u3 is absorbing with an unrewarded self-loop; there are no positive rewards to farm and no dense progress rewards are appropriate since the task requires no progress. FINAL_STATES is present and correct: u0, u1, u2 are declared safe/accepting states (doing at most one of the two satisfies the task), and this is consistent with the episode boundary — the only early termination is the box pickup, which necessarily implies both achievements and thus passes through non-accepting u3, so acceptance at step-limit end coincides exactly with never having done both. Format matches the paper artifact: REWARD_MACHINE header, declared INITIAL_STATE, nonempty declared FINAL_STATES, per-state else coverage, and rewards keyed consistently as (source, label, target).

feedback: All five environment-declared propositions are implemented, with no extra functions and none missing. Verification per function: (1) blocker_moved — scans the grid for the unique door and checks the start-side cell (x-1, y) for a ball; with exactly one door this is equivalent to the documented cell (dx-1, dy). It is a correct non-latching condition: true when the ball is picked up (not on the grid) or dropped elsewhere, false again if the ball is dropped back on that cell. Out-of-bounds access at x-1 is safe since Grid.get returns None. (2) has_door_key — matches the documented expression exactly (carrying a key matching the door's color); persistent current-state check. (3) door_open — matches the documented expression exactly (any open door); persistent. (4) target_picked_up — matches the documented expression exactly (carrying the box named by env.mission); persistent. (5) key_lost — correctly implemented as an event: reads previous_valuation read-only, requires previous has_door_key true, current has_door_key false (inline re-evaluation is character-identical to the has_door_key body), and current door_open false (identical to the door_open body); false on every other step, so it does not linger after the drop. The truthiness guard on previous_valuation is harmless since it is always a complete non-empty valuation. No imports, no actions, no mutations of env or episode_memory; only documented API surface (env.grid.get, env.width/height, env.carrying, env.mission, cell.type/color/is_open, previous_valuation). All functions are syntactically valid Python returning booleans. Pairwise constraints hold: key_lost excludes has_door_key and door_open by construction, and its drop-step requirement keeps it disjoint from target_picked_up. Unused-by-RM propositions (door_open, target_picked_up, key_lost) are correctly present since the declared set must be complete.
